courses.title: Barrio Organization and Service Learning
courses.description: Seminar, two hours; discussion, two hours; field placement, six hours. Limited to juniors/seniors. Service learning placement in community-based organization, labor union, or service-oriented nonprofit organization. Study of role that these organizations play in improvement and change of Chicana/Chicano communities. Students meet on regular basis with instructors and provide periodic reports… For more content click the Read More button below.

courses.title: Theoretical Concepts in Chicana/Chicano Studies
courses.description: (Formerly numbered Chicana and Chicano Studies 101.) Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour. Requisite: course 10A or 10B. Survey of different theoretical approaches to field of Chicana and Chicano studies. Letter grading.

courses.title: Comedy and Culture: Your Humorous Life
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. How to mine unique humorous life adventures from students’ cultural identities and turn those distinct experiences into humorous literature. Students acquire skills to read their stories out loud, with emphasis on comedy in their pieces through art of storytelling and performance. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Chicana/Chicano Folklore
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Examination of roots of Chicana/Chicano folklore in Mexican oral tradition in mid-19th century and development of Chicana/Chicano folklore to present day. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Introduction to Chicana/Chicano Studies: History and Culture
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Interdisciplinary survey of diverse historical experiences, cultural factors, and ethnic/racial paradigms, including indigenousness, gender, sexuality, language, and borders, that help shape Chicana/Chicano identities. Emphasis on critical reading and writing skills. Letter grading.

courses.title: Introduction to Chicana/Chicano Studies: Social Structure and Contemporary Conditions
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Multidisciplinary examination of representation, ideologies, and material conditions of Chicanas/Chicanos, including colonialism, race, labor, immigration, poverty, assimilation, and patriarchy. Emphasis on critical reading and writing skills. Letter grading.

courses.title: Chicana/Chicano and Latina/Latino Intellectual Traditions
courses.description: Lecture, five hours. General view of philosophical, cultural, and social thought as well as intellectual traditions in Americas. Roles of writers as intellectuals and cultural/political strategists, and as definers of (national) identity, social reality, and struggles of liberation. Letter grading.

courses.title: Chicana/Chicano Images in Mexican Film and Literature
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Preparation: adequate understanding of Spanish-language films without English subtitles. Throughout its rich history, spanning more than 100 years, Mexican cinema has produced great variety of films that deal with Chicana/Chicano experience. courses.title: Immigration and Chicano Community
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Discussion on relationship between international immigration and development of Chicana/Chicano community. Examination of U.S. immigration policy and relationship between Mexican-origin population and other Latin American immigrants. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Applied Research Methods in Latino Communities
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Through combination of lectures, key readings, and several experiments, introduction to several applied research methods that are highly effective in producing sound and methodologically rigorous studies on poor and/or Latino communities, including important data that can be used for critical analysis and policy recommendations. Letter grading.

courses.title: Barrio Popular Culture
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Construction of model by which to organize study of Chicana/Chicano popular culture by focusing on barrio as metaphor for community. Examination of beliefs, myths, and values of Chicana/Chicano culture and representations in icons, heroes, legends, stereotypes, and popular art forms through literature, film, video, music, mass media,… For more content click the Read More button below.

courses.title: Mesoamerican Literature
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Preparation: reading knowledge of Spanish (level 4). Survey of premises of Mesoamerican literatures, including myths, lyrics, poetry, religious celebrations, rituals, and drama, specifically of Aztec and Mayan peoples prior to European contact. Letter grading.

courses.title: Mestizaje: History of Diverse Racial/Cultural Roots of Mexico
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Historical examination of diverse racial and cultural roots of Chicanas and Chicanos. Utilizing theoretical frameworks of mestizaje, Aztlán, indigenismo, La Raza Cósmica, and la tercera raíz, examination of some important groups who have contributed to formation of Mexican national culture. Development of… For more content click the Read More button below.

courses.title: Literature of Chicana/Chicano Movement
courses.description: (Formerly numbered M145B.) Lecture, three hours. Examination of literature of Chicana/Chicano movement covering period from first manifestations of Chicano artistic production in 1965 with el Teatro Campesino through rise of women’s writing, including work by Cherrie Moraga (1983), Helena Maria Viramontes (1985), and Sandra Cisneros (1991). P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Chicano Narrative
courses.description: (Formerly numbered M146.) Lecture, three hours. Introduction to major Chicano narrative genres—novel, romance, satire, autobiography, cronicón/semblanza, Chicana detective novel, and Chicana solidarity fiction. Texts examined within their own geographic, cultural, and historical contexts, as well as within history of narrative forms. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Gendered Politics and Chicana/Latina Political Participation
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Examination of Chicanas and Latinas as participants, organizers, and leaders in communities, workplaces, labor unions, and government. Survey of Chicanas/Latinas in politics and as policymakers in appointed and elected offices. Analysis of gendering of politics and political behavior. Letter grading.

courses.title: Affirmative Action: History and Politics
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Historical examination of political economic context in which affirmative action policies and programs were conceived and implemented. Review of impact on Chicanas/Chicanos, Latinas/Latinos, and other communities. Specific analysis of university admissions, hiring and contracting practices, and state initiatives. Letter grading.

courses.title: Human Rights in Americas
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. courses.title: Disposable People: U.S. Deportation and Repatriation Campaigns
courses.description: Seminar, four hours. Examination of U.S. deportation campaigns targeted at Mexican, Central American, and other Latin American workers, residents, and U.S.-born citizens. courses.title: Central Americans in U.S.
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Interdisciplinary survey of social, historical, political, economic, educational, and cultural experiences of Central American immigrants and their children in U.S. Introduction to several contemporary experiences and issues in U.S. Central American communities. courses.title: Chicano Movement and Its Political Legacies
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Collective examination of Chicano Movement of 1960s and 1970s and analysis of its political legacies. Grounded in historiographic inquiry and social movement theory, investigation of mobilization of diverse sectors of el movimiento, including students, workers, artists, youth, community activists, and women. courses.title: Bilingual Advantage: Spanish Language Topics on Chicana/Chicano and Latin American Cultures

Comparison with Spanish language mass media in other parts of world. Letter grading.

courses.title: Latinas and Latinos in Public Education
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Examination of language issues pertinent to educational systems, including language inequity, literacy, testing, and socialization, as well as institutional ideologies. Letter grading.

courses.title: Paulo Freire for Chicana/Chicano Classroom
courses.description: Seminar, four hours. Introduction to pedagogy of Paulo Freire and examination of historical and contemporary problems circumscribing Chicana/Chicano education. courses.title: Latinos: Print Media

courses.title: Representations of Indigenous Peoples in Americas

courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, three hours. Course 174AX is enforced requisite to 174BX. courses.title: History of Chicana/Chicano Los Angeles, 20th Century
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. History of Mexican American people in 20th-century Los Angeles. Readings and lectures emphasize formation of regional identity among Mexican Americans in Los Angeles and their significance to emergence of multicultural metropolis. Letter grading.

courses.title: History of U.S./Mexican Borderlands
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Survey of historic and geographic diversity of Chicana/Chicano identity and culture, with emphasis on regional communities of California, New Mexico, and Texas in Spanish/Mexican borderlands as situated within U.S. national context. Letter grading.

courses.title: Variable Topics Research Seminars: Chicana/o and Central American Studies
courses.description: Seminar, three hours. Limited to juniors/seniors. Research seminar organized around readings and engaged discussion of critical topic of interest in field. courses.title: Honors Research in Chicana/Chicano and Central American Studies: Thesis Conceptualization

courses.title: Honors Research in Chicana/Chicano and Central American Studies: Annotated Bibliography/Literature Review
courses.description: Tutorial, one hour. Requisite: course 198A. Limited to junior/senior honors program students. courses.title: Directed Research or Senior Project in Chicana/Chicano and Central American Studies
courses.description: Tutorial, two hours. Limited to juniors/seniors. Supervised individual research or investigation under guidance of faculty mentor. Culminating paper or project required. May be repeated for credit. Individual contract required. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Chicana and Latin American Women's Narrative
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Preparation: reading knowledge of Spanish (level 4). courses.title: Language Politics and Policies in U.S.: Comparative History
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. courses.description: (Same as Gender Studies M135C and Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer Studies M135.) Seminar, four hours. Limited to juniors/seniors. courses.title: Transnational Women's Organizing in Americas
courses.description: (Same as Gender Studies M147C.) Lecture, four hours. Feminist theories of transnational organizing. courses.title: Origins and Evolution of Chicano Theater

courses.title: Contemporary Chicano Theater: Beginning of Chicano Theater Movement

courses.description: (Same as Theater M103G.) Lecture, three hours. Analysis and discussion of Chicano theater since 1980, including discussion of Chicana playwrights, magic realism, Chicano comedy, and Chicano performance art. Letter grading.

courses.title: Early Chicana/Chicano Literature, 1400 to 1920

courses.description: (Same as English M105C.) Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Enforced requisite: English Composition 3. courses.description: (Same as Ethnomusicology M108A.) Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour. Survey of traditional and contemporary musical culture. P/NP or letter grading.
